newsitem.title: USA: Columbia Labs sees profitability in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Columbia Labs sees profitability in 1997.

text.p: Columbia Laboratories Inc, reporting a sharply higher net loss for the fiscal year ended December 31, said Monday it expects to be profitable in 1997 as its Crinone product gathers momentum in the marketplace.

Columbia Labs said it received its first purchase order from Wyeth-Ayerst, a unit of American Home Products Corp, to produce Crinone for the U.S. launch. Crinone is vaginally delivered natural progesterone.
"The anticipated timely approval of Crinone by the FDA and the subsequent sales of the product by Wyeth-Ayerst are expected to make Columbia profitable in 1997," the company said in a press release.
In addition to revenue from Crinone sales, the company said it expects to receive over $6 million in milestone payments from Wyeth-Ayerst in the coming months.

Columbia Laboratories reported a net loss of $13,078,984, or $0.47 per share, for its 1996 fiscal year, compared with a net loss of $959,472, or $0.04 per share, in 1995. Sales in 1996 were $5,646,031, compared with $9,904,633 in 1995.
